newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed, PGMs stay firm.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed, PGMs stay firm.

text.p: The platinum group metals continued to set the pace in the precious metals sector on Wendesday afternoon but the gold and silver markets were reluctant followers, dealers said.

Silver was largely unmoved by a fairly bullish Silver Institute report which showed demand outrunning supply for the eighth straight year and gold was close to the $350.00 per ounce resistance which had thwarted progress already this week.
Bullion was fixed at $349.10 per ounce up just 10 cents from the morning fixing and against $348.90 on Tuesday afternoon.
Comex June gold was down $0.30 at $350.20 at the fix.
"There is just too much producer and fund selling at $350.00 for gold to get much further. It is really the platinum group metals that are keeping it up there," one dealer said.
The other factor helping gold was the weaker dollar which was lower after a shock 0.6-percent drop in the U.S. April Producer Price Index. Economists had forecast a flat return.
It was the heftiest fall in the PPI since August, 1993 and helped pull the dollar back under 119 yen but it held around 1.70 mark on the foreign exchange markets.
However dealers also noted that a lower PPI was deeply non-inflationary which was not constructive for gold.
It also suggested less need to raise U.S. interest rates later this month which could have raised gold's atractiveness to investors versus paper assets, they said.
Lustreless silver was around $4.86/$4.88, up two cents.
Dealers said there were no real surprises in the 1997 World Silver Survey carried out for the Silver Institute by Gold Fields Mineral Services.

Supply of silver from mines and scrap rose modestly but not enough to satisfy fabrication demand of 803 million ounces requiring withdrawals from silver investories. World stocks of silver have been reduced by about 540 million ounces since the end of 1990, the survey said.
Meanwhile dealers said the rampantly high platinum and palladium markets were providing most of the sector's support.
"If the PGMs were $20-$30 lower, gold would be back in the mid $330s," one dealer said.

Several dealers mentioned the markets being firmer now than on Monday when Russian officials announced they had opened export contract talks with Japanese trade houses after a delay of over five months.
Platinum was indicated at $394.00/$395.00, up $6.00 and palladium was $5.00 firmer at $175.00/$176.00.
